ruleset.name: qml4j-unused
ruleset.description:
Dead-declaration guard for what Checkstyle can't analyse: unused private fields/methods and write-without-read (dead stores). These are reliable -- they don't depend on whole-program / functional-interface analysis.
NOT here: - unused parameters: a syntactic tool can't tell a parameter is a functional-interface contract (e.g. a private method bound via `this::m` as a MemberEmitter), so it false-positives on dispatch methods. Parameter analysis is delegated to ECJ (Eclipse compiler), wired as a check-only verify step -- see the `ecj` profile in the parent POM. - unused locals: already covered by Checkstyle's UnusedLocalVariable. - unused public members/types: qml4j is a published library; "unused" can't be decided here (consumed externally).
